sections.h2: What a PO and a GRN each commit you to
paras: A purchase order is a commitment to buy at an agreed rate. A goods receipt note is the record that the goods actually arrived, in what quantity and condition. The useful software behaviour is that the second one automatically does two things at once: it puts the received quantity into the right stock location, and it opens a payable against the supplier for what was received.

Aura Business handles this in the Procurement and Suppliers suite, through the Supplier Master, Supplier Price Lists, Purchase Orders, PO Approval Workflow, Goods Receipt and Supplier Payments. Because purchasing and inventory are the same system, a short delivery is visible as a short delivery rather than as a mysterious difference discovered at the next stock count.

sections.h2: Purchasing errors are quiet until the supplier's statement arrives.
sections.lead: Sales mistakes get found by customers. Purchase mistakes get found by accountants, months later.

items.p: A purchase is agreed in a chat with no document, so there is nothing to check the invoice against.
The supplier bills at a higher rate than agreed and there is no price list to point at.
A large order is placed by someone who did not need to ask anyone, and the money is already spent.
Nine of ten cartons arrive, the paperwork says ten, and the difference becomes a stock loss.
Goods sit in the godown for a week before anyone enters them, so sales quote from a stale figure.
What is owed to each supplier is worked out from invoices in a file rather than from receipts.

items.q: Does the GRN update stock automatically?
items.a: Yes. The quantity recorded as received enters the delivery location named on the purchase order, with serials, batches and expiry dates captured at that point, and the movement appears in the stock ledger.

items.q: What happens if only part of the order arrives?
items.a: The GRN records what actually came. The purchase order stays partly open for the balance, so the outstanding quantity is visible and can be chased or cancelled rather than forgotten.
Yes. The PO approval workflow routes orders for sign-off before they are sent, and you decide who approves what. The approval is recorded in the audit log.
Each supplier carries a price list per item, so purchase order lines are priced from the agreed rate rather than typed. Differences between the price list and the supplier invoice are then visible.

items.q: Does this handle GST on purchases?
items.a: Supplier invoices and payables are recorded with their tax detail and flow into the accounting export for your books. Input credit treatment is a matter for your accountant to confirm.

items.q: Can we buy for a specific customer order?
items.a: Yes. A purchase order can be raised against a confirmed sales order so the incoming stock is expected for that delivery. See warehouse management.
